title: The Last Static Again
premise: Ivo Underhill, a clone grown from the murdered beacon-keeper he replaced, tends a transmission beacon on the edge of the solar system that no record shows anyone commissioning. When the deep-space vessel Meridian returns with its crew aged backward into childhood, carrying a message that could reignite war between Earth's fleet and the Outer Colonies, Ivo discovers the beacon is the only thing keeping a fragile armistice broadcast alive. As he falls for Meridian's de-aged navigator, Sefa, who retains fragmented memories of the original Ivo, he learns the beacon's signal is a lie he must sustain: a fake voice of a dead peacekeeper holding two fleets apart. In the climax, Ivo must choose between broadcasting the truth—which will destroy his own identity and possibly Sefa's love for him—or letting the loop end and war resume; he splices his own living voice into the dead peacekeeper's pattern, ending the lie by making it true, and the fleets stand down as the final transmission completes.
about_author: Mara Eastwick is the pen name of a former radio engineer who spent a decade maintaining automated transmission arrays in remote northern stations before turning to fiction. She writes science fiction about people who keep machines running for audiences that may no longer exist.

chapters.title: The Commission That Never Was
chapters.summary: Ivo Underhill performs his daily maintenance on Beacon Nine, reciting the logs of a man whose murder file he inherited along with his face. He finds a maintenance order in the archive dated after the original's death—signed by the original. POV: Ivo. Beat: quiet unease, the first crack in routine.

chapters.title: Loop 4,417
chapters.summary: Ivo monitors Earth's last transmission loop, a peacekeeper's broadcast repeating on schedule, and records his nightly voice check. He notices the loop's checksum has drifted by a single character—impossible, unless someone edited it. POV: Ivo. Beat: loneliness sharpening into suspicion.

chapters.title: Return of the Meridian
chapters.summary: A ship appears at the beacon's edge, transponder dead: the Meridian, lost eleven years ago. Its crew are children—the same officers, de-aged. A girl with Sefa Voss's eyes asks Ivo if he is the man from the photographs she keeps dreaming of. POV: Ivo. Beat: awe curdling into dread.

chapters.title: The Navigator's Dreams
chapters.summary: Sefa, biologically nine but carrying fragmented adult memories, describes the original Ivo's last hours as if she witnessed them. Ivo realizes her de-aging preserved memories the murderer wanted erased. POV: Sefa. Beat: disorientation and a child's terrible clarity.

chapters.title: Two Fleets, One Silence
chapters.summary: Ivo briefs the child-captain, Ade Okafor, on the armistice: Earth's fleet and the Outer Colonies stand down only because the peacekeeper's voice still broadcasts. Ade reveals the Meridian was sent to find the loop's source—and it never answered their hails. POV: Ade. Beat: the weight of command in small hands.

chapters.title: What the Original Knew
chapters.summary: Digging into the murder file, Ivo finds the original discovered the beacon was commissioned covertly by both fleets as a shared lie—a fake peacekeeper, since the real one died in the first war. The original was killed for knowing. POV: Ivo. Beat: grief for a man whose life he is wearing.

chapters.title: Checksum
chapters.summary: Sefa's memories help Ivo trace the corrupted checksum: someone aboard the Meridian, before de-aging, altered the loop to end it early. The saboteur is now a child who doesn't remember doing it. POV: Sefa. Beat: betrayal without a betrayer.

chapters.title: The Child Who Signed
chapters.summary: Ivo identifies engineer Tam Rell, now six years old, whose adult self was a Colony agent. Confronting a child with a crime they cannot recall, Ivo hesitates—and Tam's terror triggers a hidden failsafe in the Meridian's systems. POV: Tam. Beat: compassion at war with duty.

chapters.title: Hail from Earth
chapters.summary: Earth's fleet arrives, demanding the Meridian's surrender as a Colony vessel. Ade must claim beacon jurisdiction neither fleet recognizes. Ivo, for the first time, speaks to Earth command using the peacekeeper's voice protocol—and they obey. POV: Ade. Beat: the intoxicating and corrupting taste of borrowed authority.

chapters.title: The Colony Answers
chapters.summary: The Outer Colonies' fleet jumps in, responding to the same voice. Both sides hold, waiting for orders from a dead man. Ivo realizes he is now the only person alive both fleets trust. POV: Ivo. Beat: vertigo of accidental power.

chapters.title: Orders from a Dead Man
chapters.summary: Earth's admiral privately pressures Ivo to use the voice to order the Colony fleet's disarmament—a move that would end the balance and hand Earth victory. He offers Ivo a real identity, a real name, a life off the beacon. POV: Ivo. Beat: temptation dressed as rescue.

chapters.title: What Sefa Remembers of Love
chapters.summary: Sefa, aging unnaturally fast as her de-aging reverses, recalls loving the original Ivo and confesses she cannot tell whether her feelings are hers or a dead man's echo. Ivo admits he is a copy. They choose each other anyway, knowing neither is the person who began this. POV: Sefa. Beat: love chosen against uncertainty.

chapters.title: The Loop Ends
chapters.summary: The failsafe Tam triggered completes its work: the transmission loop terminates. Both fleets, hearing silence, begin arming. Ivo has hours, not days. POV: Ade. Beat: countdown pressure, panic in the ranks.

chapters.title: Tam's Confession
chapters.summary: Under Sefa's gentle questioning, child-Tam recovers a buried memory: the adult Rell was ordered to end the loop by someone inside Earth command itself—the war faction. The saboteur had an accomplice still on Earth, feeding the admiral's ambitions. POV: Tam. Beat: a child carrying an adult's guilt.

chapters.title: The Admiral's Truth
chapters.summary: Ivo confronts the admiral with Tam's memory records. The admiral doesn't deny it—he argues the armistice was always a lie, and a lie maintained by a clone is the most obscene lie of all. Ivo cannot refute him. POV: Ivo. Beat: the enemy makes the strongest moral argument.

chapters.title: Broadcast Rights
chapters.summary: Sefa proposes the impossible: instead of faking the peacekeeper, Ivo should broadcast as himself—a clone, telling both fleets the whole truth, the murder included. Ade warns it will be read as Colony propaganda or Earth trickery. They prepare anyway. POV: Sefa. Beat: hope that requires courage, not certainty.

chapters.title: Voice Print
chapters.summary: Ivo records his testimony: the original's murder, the beacon's false commission, the admiral's faction, his own clonehood. Splicing his living voice into the dead peacekeeper's pattern, he makes the lie true—the peacekeeper's voice continues, but it is a real person confessing. POV: Ivo. Beat: self-annihilation as authorship.

chapters.title: The Transmission
chapters.summary: The broadcast goes out on all channels. Both fleets receive a dead man's cadence carrying a clone's confession. The Colony fleet stands down first; Earth's wavers as the admiral's faction fractures, officers refusing to fire on a voice they were raised to obey. POV: Ade. Beat: climax—the lie's death and the truth's survival in one signal.

chapters.title: Mutiny of the Obedient
chapters.summary: Earth's war faction attempts to seize the beacon. The child crew of the Meridian defends it, and Earth's own officers, hearing Ivo's loop still repeating his confession, turn their weapons on the mutineers. The admiral surrenders rather than fire on children. POV: Tam. Beat: loyalty inverted, violence refused.

chapters.title: After the Silence
chapters.summary: Both fleets establish a joint commission at Beacon Nine—the first institution both sides have ever shared. Ivo is offered command and refuses; he asks instead to be listed in the logs as what he is: the second Underhill, keeper of the first's grave. POV: Ivo. Beat: humility after power.

chapters.title: Aged Forward
chapters.summary: Sefa's aging stabilizes at twenty-six, her memories integrating—neither the woman who left nor the child who returned, but someone new. She and Ivo, both second versions of other people's lives, begin a first version of their own. POV: Sefa. Beat: tenderness earned through loss.

chapters.title: The Next Commission
chapters.summary: One year later, the beacon transmits a new loop: not a lie, but an archive—the full record of the Meridian, the murder, and the peace, broadcast for whoever comes next. Ivo signs the maintenance order himself, dated today. POV: Ivo. Beat: resolution—memory kept honestly at last.
